civV7.isCivRaw (:2258): speaks or learns, not GOOD or EVIL, not an animal person of a non-vermin root, and has a SUBTERRANEAN biome
1.5 Ecology class and locking
  • V7.ecologyClassRaw (:1588-1615) sorts each raw into one class, testing in this order:
    • generated (GENERATED);
    • mega (MEGABEAST, SEMIMEGABEAST, TITAN);
    • night (the NIGHT_CREATURE_* flags);
    • unliving (NOT_LIVING, or NO_EAT + NO_DRINK without GRAZER or CARNIVORE);
    • mythic (FANCIFUL, GOOD, EVIL);
    • unclassified (no body size, or no BIOME);
    • natural (everything else).
  • ecoOf (:1678-1688): a player override can only bring a creature in as natural. A mythic creature becomes natural through V7.alignedNatural (:1657) in three cases:
    • FANCIFUL alone, when v7 fanciful is on;
    • a cave-only GOOD or EVIL species, when cave_aligned is on;
    • surface GOOD or EVIL wildlife on a region of its own alignment, when aligned is on. V7.alignment (:1620) reads each region tile's evilness: < 33 is good, ≥ 66 is evil; the world_region's own flags count too.
  • e.locked = cfg.classes[eco] ~= true (:2360). The defaults (:818) manage only natural.
    • A locked species is never allowed (isAllowed :2417).
    • V7.sanitizeLocked (:1742) drops a saved allow or assign for one at load.
  • defaultAllow(e) = in the embark, not HAS_ANY_MEGABEAST or night, and not locked (:2416).
1.6 Savagery
  • Per species: e.savage is the raw SAVAGE flag (:1816). No roster builder filters on it. A SAVAGE species is in the pool whenever DF stocked it.
  • Per map: ROSTER.savage(cfg) (:7642-7665) reads each region tile's savagery. The map counts as savage if any tile is at or above roster.apex.savage_cut (default 66). It sets:
    • the builder's land APX slot maximum to 2 (:7770);
    • the apex scheduler's cap: cap_savage instead of cap_calm (:8905).
  • SAVAGE on a calm map (R36): addNewSpecies (:4008) calls ROSTER.invasiveAdded (:8929). For a SAVAGE raw on a calm map, it places one group at once from the new entries' stock (ROSTER.placeGroup) and lists the species in roster.invasive. ROSTER.placeTick (:8915-8923) then keeps placing it toward apex.invasive_presence (25%).
1.7 Animal people and giants

They are pool members like any other. The rosters weigh them down:

At pick timeOnce seated (FREQUENCY)
Builder (ROSTER.pickWeight :7829)AP that is not civ ×ap_pick 0.1; else giant ×giant_pick 0.2ROSTER.ladder :7906: AP ×ap_freq 0.25, giant ×giant_freq 0.5, inside the trophic level
Casts (castGrow weight :8472)AP that is not civ ×roster.ap_pick 0.1; giant ×cast.giant 0.2 (a separate knob)the casts write no FREQUENCY
  • ROSTER.boosted (:7672): with giant_boost on, a predator-guild GIANT_* is an apex (APX) whatever its mass.
  • ROSTER.freqFloorApply (:8952): an in-embark animal person whose raw FREQUENCY is 0 is written ap_freq_floor (1), so DF can draw it at all. This runs from V7.apply on every enable.
1.8 Extinct creatures

The pool adds no extinct species of its own. The 200 extinct creatures are in the pool only where worldgen gave them regional populations (comment :13900-13906).

V7.EXTINCT (:13939-14069) is an 83-row correction table, checked in this pass with Python:

  • 21 FREQUENCY rows (apexes at 50, 100 or 30 brought to 2-5);
  • 23 STANDARD_GRAZER rows;
  • role rows (Titanoboa, Dimetrodon, Tiktaalik, Eoraptor);
  • 3 cluster rows;
  • fossil realms.

The model reads it at classify time (§1.4). The raws are written in V7.EXTINCT.apply (:14222). The builder's apex FREQUENCY also reads the corrected value before it is written (:7944-7950).

1.9 Vermin

Vermin are in the pool (cat = 'vermin') but never fill a trophic slot (ROSTER.inPart :7721 excludes them).

  • Builder: a vermin draw for the GOBBLE edge table only (ROSTER.gobbleEdges :8007), at most gobble_max (3) per class per layer.
  • Casts: 2-3 vermin per cast that a cast member eats (§3.5).
  • Vermin class ROSTER.vclass (:7982), from VERMIN.family (:3222):
ClassFamily
VFfish. Since 29a8a91, this also covers IMMOBILE_LAND or CANNOT_BREATHE_AIR vermin: guppy, clown loach, knifefish
VCcolony
VBflying vermin that are small birds or mammals
VIother flying vermin, and flies
VGeverything else
1.10 Which layer a species belongs to: ROSTER.inPart(cfg, e, layer) (:7720-7737)

No species is in a part unless it is in the embark, not locked, not vermin, and not mega or night.

Roster partMembers
caverncavern-layer entries that are not lava-only, inside the raw depth range at one or more of their cave depths (ROSTER.depthOk :7711: raw depth = layer_depth + 1; depth_near widens it by one), or with no depth recorded
waterevery water-layer entry, plus land-layer entries that are aquatic, or semiaquatic and on the curated list as apex/pelagic, or curated fishers when v7 fishers is on
flyingland-layer fliers and waterbirds
landthe rest of the land layer
(deep)never a roster part (R60)
1.11 Depth and lava guards
  • fireOnly species are out of the cavern part (:7723).
  • PLACE.fromEntry refuses deep entries and cavern entries outside raw depth (:4899-4905).
  • ROSTER.placeGroup does the same (:8753, :8761-8764) and puts lava-only species only beside magma (ROSTER.magmaSide :8729), or refuses.
  • ROSTER.placeBorrowed (:9030) is the opt-in roster depth place path.
1.12 Realms (v7 realms, off by default)
  • V7.REALMS (:2040-2154) is a curated table of real-world ranges. It can be extended by dfhack-config/seasonal-wildlife-realms.json and by the extinct fossil realms.
  • V7.realmOk (:2202) is applied only by the builder (ROSTER.candidatesFor :7854, with cfg.realm resolved at :8073-8078). COS is always allowed, and OCE is allowed on the water part.
  • The casts do not apply realms.

2. The guild builder, ROSTER.build(cfg, layer) (:8064-8256)

2.1 Slot tables

ROSTER.SLOTS (:7740-7749) sets min-max per slot. ROSTER.slotTable (:7766) then adjusts them to the map:

PartSlots (min-max)Map adjustments
landAPX 1-1, GZ 1-2, PL 1-2, ML 1-2, SH 0-1APX 1-2 on a savage map (:7770)
flyingAPX 0-1, RP 1-1, LB 1-2, WB 0-2(R50: one raptor slot)
waterAPX 1-1, APE 0-0, FC 1-3, FF 1-2, SH 1-2, MW 0-1, PE 0-1, WB 0-1ocean on the map: APE 1-1, PE 1-1, or PE 1-2 when a deep column exists (:7772-7773)
cavernAPX 1-1, PL 1-3, ML 0-2, RP 0-1, LB 0-1, SH 0-2, MW 0-1, FF 0-2APX max = number of cavern depths the part's species occupy (:7771)
any+ SN 0-1, SNP 0-1only with roster.sn_slots on (off by default) (:7776-7778)

ROSTER.context (:7752) reads the map facts behind these adjustments:

  • savage from ROSTER.savage;
  • ocean: any ocean tile (ENGINE.waterTiles().sum.ocean > 0);
  • deep: ENGINE.deepColumns(cfg).n > 0, meaning at least one sampled ocean column holding water.column_levels (3) stacked water tiles at level ≥ 4/7;
  • the cavern depths present.
2.2 How a species gets its slot: ROSTER.slotOf(cfg, e, layer) (:7685-7705)

The rules are tested in this order:

  1. Cavern civ race with civ_prey on: AL or AW becomes ML, or MW when aquatic. A civ race never holds an apex slot.
  2. sn_slots on, sentient and not a monster: SN (tier ≥ 2) or SNP.
  3. Water part:
    • the curated aquatic_apex kind pelagic → APE;
    • apex or fisher → APX;
    • any other AW, AL or ML → MW (R49 demotes the sea lamprey);
    • otherwise the guild.
  4. Flying part: APX if ROSTER.flyApex (:7679) holds: an RP that is not sentient, not a cave species, not a scavenger (vulture, buzzard, kea, raven), with mass ≥ fly_apex_min (2000) or boosted. Otherwise the guild.
  5. Land and cavern parts: AL, AW or boosted → APX; otherwise the guild.

Tiers (ROSTER.TIER :7667): APX, APE, AL and AW are 3; ML, MW, RP and SN are 2; every other guild is 1; V is 0. Trophic level (ROSTER.LEVEL :7668): apex slots are A, ML/MW/RP/SN are C, everything else is H.

2.3 Which pairs count as a food link: ROSTER.linkable(e, p, cfg, layer) (:7794)

Three tests must all pass:

  • e's tier is strictly above p's;
  • MODEL.reaches(e, p) holds (:2565): neither is mega or night, p is not a sponge, the same ecology class, the same realm (surface or cavern), the habitat REACH table (:2531) allows it, and shared water when both are aquatic;
  • in the caverns, the two share a cavern depth.

There is no size test. Size enters only through preference() in the pick weight.

2.4 Seed and pick weight

The weight. ROSTER.pickWeight(e, roster) (:7829-7841) is:

w = (pack ? pack_bonus : 1) × (AP not civ ? ap_pick : giant ? giant_pick : 1) × (1 + Σ preference over linkable pairs with the roster so far)

  • The pack bonus (ROSTER.packBonus :7789): tier ≥ 2, not BENIGN, and raw cmax > 1 (R41).
  • preference(e, p) (:2576): exp(−ln(M_prey / (0.4 M_pred))² / (2 × 1.2²)). Vermin score 0.05.

ROSTER.weightedPick (:7842) is a weighted random draw (rng:drandom).

The seed (:8107-8114): the first slot in table order that has candidates with any link in the layer's candidate set. The seed is a weighted pick among those candidates, against an empty roster.

2.5 Fill passes, the fallback when filling stalls, and unfilled slots
  1. Minimum pass (fillPass(false) :8116-8130). Each slot fills to its min by weighted picks from the candidates not yet used.
  2. When filling stalls (:8133-8158). If a slot is still below its min and the last pass made no progress, the builder takes the first unused candidate of that slot that links to any unused candidate p. It seats the candidate, and seats p too if p's slot has room (pairsSeeded). The loop has a 200-iteration guard.
  3. Maximum pass (while fillPass(true) :8159). Every slot fills to its max.
  4. Unfilled slots (:8161-8172). Each slot still below its min is reported with one of three reasons: `no candidate in pool, no edge in pool, or pool exhausted or no partner seated`. The builder then carries on: an unfilled slot is never fatal.
2.6 Link guard and the vegetation link (:8175-8208)

The builder repeats this step until nothing changes, with a guard of 200 rounds. A seated species with no link to any other seated species goes through three checks:

  • If it is a herbivore (level H, not CARNIVORE) and V7.vegSupports(e) holds, it stays, "kept by the vegetation link".
  • Otherwise it is swapped for an unused candidate of the same slot that does link.
  • Failing that, it is dropped.

The vegetation index is V7.vegSurvey (:7438-7505): (region vegetation mean + grass share %) / 2.

  • The region vegetation is read through getRegionBiome.
  • The grass share is the grass floor tiles over the outdoor walkable floor of the surface band.
  • Shrub and tree counts are reported but not used in the index.
  • The survey has a 1000 ms deadline and is cached per map.

The need is V7.vegSupports (:7511): need = clamp(20 + 15 × log10(mass / 100,000 cm³), 10, 90), and the species is supported when index ≥ need.

2.7 Outgun check (:8211-8224)

ROSTER.outgunPairs (:7805) finds every seated predator-prey pair where the prey is not BENIGN and the prey's mass × group is at least v7.outgun (2.0) × the predator's mass × group. Each such pair is logged as a build ledger line.

With v7 outgun_cap on (it is off by default), the builder also sets cfg.group_size[prey] to floor(predMass × factor / preyUnitMass). PATTERN.sizeApply then writes that as the raw CLUSTER_NUMBER on the next groups pass.

2.8 The FREQUENCY ladder: ROSTER.ladder(cfg, layer, members, ctx) (:7882-7971)

The builder turns the seated species into FREQUENCY values (1-100) for the prey (H) and meso-predator (C) levels. Apexes are handled separately, at step 8.

  1. Group by slot. Apex-level members (APX, APE, AL, AW) go to a separate list.
  2. Base weight for each H/C member.
    • b = LADDER22[part][slot] (:7874-7879). For SN or SNP members the code looks up their guild instead; a slot code with no entry falls back to 5.
    • On water, a PE member's b is tripled when ctx.deep (:7900).
  3. Mass scaling within its slot. scale = clamp((mass / geometric-mean mass of its slot)^−0.75, 0.25, 4) (:7901).
  4. Animal-people and giant multiplier. ×ap_freq or ×giant_freq, applied inside the level (:7906).
  5. Split between levels. The pyramid's H:C shares are normalised, from roster.pyramid[pk], where pk is ocean/lake on water (by ctx.ocean) and otherwise the part's own name.
    • If a level is empty, the other level takes 100%.
  6. Biomass guard (land and cavern only, :7918-7925). If uC × meanMass_C > guard × uH × meanMass_H (guard = 0.5), then the code sets r = guard × mH / mC, uC = r / (1 + r) and uH = 1 − uC, and reports binding = biomass guard.
  7. Unit share, then scaling to 0-100.
    • Each member gets x = levelShare × v / ΣlevelQ.
    • With roster.units on, x is divided by ROSTER.groupMean (:7862): the player's group size, else the raw cluster midpoint, not floored.
    • The result is rescaled so the largest x becomes 100, then rounded, and floored at 1 (:7935-7939).
  8. Apex members (R34: no step on the ladder).
    • apex_odds > 0 → that value is written.
    • Else a raw FREQUENCY above apex_raw_cap (5) is written as the cap.
    • Else nothing is written, and the raw's own FREQUENCY stands. The "raw" here is the snapshot's original if one is held (CAVERN.saved). An extinct apex reads its corrected value (:7944-7950).
  9. Report. info holds the targets, the binding constraint, the floored tokens, and the predicted carnivore share in waves and in units.

Default weights (ROSTER.LADDER22, :7874-7879) and pyramid targets (V7.rosterDefaults().pyramid, :7556-7558):

PartGuild weights inside a levelPyramid H / C / A (%)
landGZ 10.5, PL 8.75, SH 7, LB 6, WB 6, ML 2, MW 2, RP 273 / 20 / 7
flyingLB 30, WB 30, RP 2, ML 280 / 20 / 0
waterFC 12, FF 12, WB 9, SH 6, GZ 6, PL 6, PE 2, MW 2, ML 2ocean 82 / 13 / 5; lake 87 / 13 / 3
cavernGZ 12, LB 12, WB 12, FF 12, PL 10, SH 8, ML 2, RP 2, MW 260 / 27 / 13

The A share is not used by the ladder. Apex presence is the scheduler's job, at its own targets (§2.10).

2.9 What the build writes (:8226-8251)

For every candidate in the part whose slot is in the table but was not chosen:

  • ROSTER.setActive(..., false), if it was active;
  • cfg.odds[key] = nil.

For every member:

  • ROSTER.setActive(..., true). A member with no season gets one default season (ROSTER.defaultSeason :2675);
  • cfg.odds[key] = ladder[key];
  • apex-level keys are added to cfg.roster.apex_keys[part].

Then:

  • ROSTER.gobbleEdges builds the vermin edge table for the part;
  • one build ledger line is written;
  • the verb pushes one undo step (:18470), saves, and runs applyLive when rotation is on.

The FREQUENCY values themselves reach the raws only through CAVERN.apply (§4).

2.10 Apex scheduler (R9, R34): ROSTER.placeTick (:8893) and ROSTER.apex.decide (:8845)
  • When it runs. Once per game day from tick() (:4148-4152), for each part with apex_keys, then for the R36 invasives (:8917-8923).
  • Presence. It measures the share of time an apex group of those races is on the map, counted by population source (ROSTER.apex.groupsOnMap :8702). DF's own waves count.
  • When it stops. Reached the cap (cap_calm 1 or cap_savage 2, chosen at :8905), or at target after 7 days of observation.
  • Otherwise. It places with probability 1 − exp(−λ·dt), where λ = P / ((1 − P) × residence), P = presence % / 100 (capped at 0.95), and residence is 21,500 ticks (:8862-8867).
  • What it places. A uniform random choice among the keys that are active, in season and stocked. The group is placed by ROSTER.placeGroup (:8749), which debits stock, enters land groups at the map edge and water groups by the water-body rule, and leads the group at once.
  • Presence targets: land 25%, flying 0%, water 20%, cavern 70%.
2.11 What the builder does not do
  • It does not run on enable, on load or on any timer.
  • It does not set seasons beyond the one default.
  • It does not touch other parts.
  • Its realm filter, ladder and apex keys are not used by the casts.

3. The v7.3 season casts (commits 64f9972 .. 09ab266, 7-8 Oct)

3.1 The rule

The header at :8259-8277 sets out the rule. The pool (the embark's species) is not the roster.

  • Each season, the tool grows a cast for each of the three roster layers (land, water, cavern).
  • The cast is that season's roster. A cast species is active in the seasons it is cast in.
  • Every other species those layers manage rests: inactive, with no season.
  • Only species that have a season may be on the map.
3.2 The cast layers and their slots (ROSTER.CAST :8282-8297)
LayerParts mergedSlots (want)Total slotsVermin
landland + flyingapex (APX) 1; meso (ML) 2; raptor (RP, or a flying APX recoded FAPX) 1; grazer (GZ) 2; ground prey (PL, SH) 2; bird (LB, WB) 1; sentient (SN, SNP) 1103
waterwaterapex (APX, APE) 1; meso (MW) 1; fish (FC, FF) 3; pelagic (PE) 1; shore (SH) 2; waterbird (WB, LB) 1; sentient 1102
caverncavernapex (APX) 1; meso (ML, MW) 2; ground prey (PL, GZ, FF) 3; flier (RP, LB) 1; shore (SH) 1; sentient 193

So a cast holds at most 13, 12 or 12 species, vermin included. With sn_slots off, the sentient slot can never fill (problem P7), so the real ceiling is 12, 11 and 11. The header (:8276-8277) records the desk's means: land 8.8 + 2.7 vermin, water 8.2 + 2.0, cavern 9.0 + 2.8.

3.3 The season's candidates: ROSTER.castPool(cfg, pool, layer, season) (:8388-8414)

Non-vermin.

  • Every entry in the layer's parts (ROSTER.inPart) qualifies, unless the raw has NO_<season> for this season (e.noSeason).
  • Each candidate gets its cast slot and code from ROSTER.castSlot (:8373), which uses slotOf on its own part. A code that no cast slot names leaves the candidate with no slot.

Vermin (castVerminOk :8379):

  • cavern: cavern-layer vermin;
  • water: water-layer vermin, plus land-layer VF vermin;
  • land: land-layer vermin that are not VF.

Since 29a8a91 there is one candidate per species token, with the layer's own entry taken first (:8402-8412). A mussel with both a water and a land entry no longer fills both vermin slots.

3.4 Who eats whom, and who can never be cast

ROSTER.castEats(a, b) (:8416-8429).

  • A vermin eats nothing.
  • If b is vermin, a eats it when ROSTER.vdiet(a.e, a.code, a.part) covers b's class. ROSTER.VDIET (:7980):
    • ML eats VG, VC and VF; MW eats VF; an aquatic APX eats VF; RP eats VB and VI;
    • a cavern LB eats VB, VI and VG;
    • vermin-root animal people eat VG, VI and VF;
    • DF's own gobblers eat VG and VC.
  • Otherwise a eats b under the builder's link rule: a higher tier, MODEL.reaches, and a shared cavern depth. Each species takes its tier from its own part, so a raptor (flying part) can take ground prey (land part).

ROSTER.castExcluded (:8431). A species is never castable this season if:

  • it has no cast slot; or
  • none of its food-web neighbours is castable. This check is repeated until stable.
3.5 Growing one cast: ROSTER.castGrow(cfg, pool, layer, season, prev, r) (:8451-8566)
  1. The food web. Build eats and the undirected neighbour map nb over every pair of candidates.
  2. The weight of a candidate (:8472-8479): 1 × cast.pack (3) if packBonus holds × cast.carry (0.25) if it was in the previous season's cast × cast.giant (0.2) if a giant × roster.ap_pick (0.1) if an animal person that is not civ. Unlike the builder, there is no preference sum over links.
  3. The seed (:8495-8507). A weighted pick among non-vermin, non-excluded candidates for which ROSTER.highValue holds; if there are none, a weighted pick among all of them. ROSTER.highValue (:8349-8371) counts a species as high-value for any of:
    • pet value ≥ cast.hv_petvalue (200). For a giant, the root animal's pet value is read (DF gives every giant 500);
    • training: TRAINABLE_WAR or TRAINABLE_HUNTING;
    • parts: mass ≥ cast.hv_mass (1,000,000 cm³), or a creature material named IVORY, PEARL, SILK or SHELL.

The answer is memoized in CACHE.hv by token.

  1. Growth (:8509-8530), with a guard of 400 rounds:
    • Pick a random member that has not been set aside.
    • Its candidates are its neighbours that are not vermin, not already cast, not excluded, and whose slot still has room.
    • If it has none, set it aside.
    • Otherwise take the candidates whose slot has the largest fractional room (the emptiest slot first). Among those, make a weighted pick, and log FROM -> TO (slot, its prey | its predator).
    • Stop when every slot is full, or every member is set aside.
  2. Unfilled slots (:8531-8538): "have of want: none in season in the pool" or `"no link to the cast from the N in the pool"`.
  3. Vermin (:8540-8561). Take the vermin that cast members eat, shuffled with r:
    • first, one per distinct class;
    • then by how many members eat them;
    • up to L.vermin in all.
  4. Edges (:8562-8565): every cast-to-cast eats pair, kept as {PRED, PREY} tokens.
3.6 A year of casts: ROSTER.castYear(cfg, pool, year, why) (:8589-8633)

Growing the casts. For each layer that cfg.layers has on (land, water, cavern; deep never), for s = 0..3:

  • The random seed is fixed by seed = (site_id × 7919 + year × 104729 + s × 131 + #layer × 17 + cast.salt) % 2147483647 (:8602), so the same fort, year and salt always grow the same casts.
  • Carry-over: prev for spring is the stored winter cast for that layer (:8599-8600). Each later season uses the season before it.

Writing the roster. For every pool entry that a cast layer manages (ROSTER.castManages :8576 — its parts and vermin, and also locked or unpartitioned species of that layer, so that BLOOD_MAN and ELEMENTMAN_MUD rest instead of leaking in at their raw odds):

CaseWhat castYear writes
cast in ≥ 1 seasonallow = true, assign = those seasons, why cast <why>
cast in no seasonallow = false, assign = nil, why resting: in no cast this year; a locked one also goes into casts.rest (:8618-8625)

casts.rest matters because V7.sanitizeLocked drops a locked key from allow at load. ROSTER.managedKey (:2723) treats keys in casts.rest as held, so applyLive and holdOutOfSeason keep their stock at 0. CAVERN.apply (:3716-3724) holds their FREQUENCY.

The result is stored as cfg.casts = {year, built = absTick, layers = {land = {[1..4] = cast}, ...}, rest}, and a season ledger line is written.

3.7 What "resting" means on each layer
LayerLeverCode
land, waterstock: every entry's quantity = 0 and flags.extinct = true. The old quantity is remembered in the RESERVE (site data seasonal-wildlife/reserve), at the season apply and again by the daily holdapplyLive :3027-3067, holdOutOfSeason :3072-3092
water (the tool's own draw)ENGINE.candidates draws only keys that ROSTER.wants (active and in season):5978-5980
cavern (and deep)raw FREQUENCY held at CAVERN.restLevelCAVERN.apply :3698-3760, CAVERN.restLevel :3683-3697

CAVERN.restLevel(cfg, token) reads cast.cavern_rest_freq (no default in CAST_DEF; nil means 1).

  • ≥ 1: that value. The comment at :3680-3682 notes that "frequency 1 still leaks ~15%".
  • 0: 0, unless the raw is vermin.
    • classify().gameVermin is one guard.
    • So is any of the creature flags VERMIN_FISH, VERMIN_SOIL_COLONY, VERMIN_ROTTER, VERMIN_GROUNDER, VERMIN_SOIL, or the caste flag VERMIN_MICRO (09ab266).
    • Vermin stay at 1 because zeroing CREEPY_CRAWLER froze DF (:3623-3630).
  • Scope. restLevel applies to any token CAVERN.apply holds while casts are on (not w.open, :3753). That includes a cavern species that is cast but out of its season, and deep-layer keys (problem P5).
3.8 When casts are built, and how they are reloaded
MomentWhat happensLine
enable / on on a fort with full_enable_roster unsetcaptureDefault; if cast.enabled (default true), every switch goes on, then castYear(..., 'enable'). The preset is skippedPANEL.fortOn :16086-16123
first frame on a fort the tool has never run onmap_loaded → PANEL.fortOn:16280-16292
every season change in a new yearV7.ST.turn calls castYear(..., 'new year') when castOn and casts.year ~= cur_year, before applyLive:4093-4110

map loadno rebuild. Since b0895b9, V7.castSanitize (:8315-8347) reads back full_enable_roster, migrated_v71, the cast switches (by type) plus cast.cavern_rest_freq, and casts (year, built, the four seasons of each layer with members, vermin and seed, the rest of each record copied as is, and rest):1058

When the season changes (34a3a4b):

  • V7.ST.arm (:4124) sets a one-shot timer for the boundary tick.
  • V7.ST.now (:4111) runs the change, retrying every 10 ticks up to 12 times until DF flips the season.
  • The groups pass (:13210-13218) is the fallback, and the daily tick (:4133) the last resort.

V7.ST.turn runs in this order: exhaustRoll, spillRoll, the new-year casts, applyLive, a ledger line, the trickle, then CAVERN.apply.

3.9 What follows the cast while it runs
  • Turnover. V7.GRP.castTurnover (:12778-12798), once per season stamp, sends off every tracked group whose key is not wanted this season. Since 8817eb4 it falls back to the land key for water groups.
  • Natives under casts. Every land and water native is adopted as a group, so the turnover can reach it, and so are flagged fish seeded from a water feature (V7.GRP.adoptNatives :12809-12822).
  • Exhaustion swap. An in-season species whose stock runs out can be swapped for a species in the same cast slot that is linked to this season's cast (ROSTER.castReplaceOk :8635). The stand-in may be a resting species; it rests again at the next change (exhaustRoll :3113). Since 6e1ffb2, exhaustion waits until applyLive has stamped CACHE.appliedStamp for this season (:3127).
  • Water spill is off under casts (:7362).
  • Ecology. Relation writes between wild pairs are kept only for this season's cast edges (ROSTER.castEdgeSet :8673, used at :5128 and :5183).
  • Nudges stay parked (V7.parkNudges :1071; PANEL.fortOn and allOn leave the parked switches off).
3.10 The cast verb (:18333-18405)
VerbEffect
cast [status]each layer and season: member count + vermin count, seed, members and vermin
cast show SEASON [LAYER]the seed and why, members by slot, vermin, unfilled slots and why, the growth log, the edges, and the never-castable species with their reasons
cast rebuild [SALT]grow this year again, with a new salt if given; apply at once
cast restfreq 0|1cast.cavern_rest_freq; runs CAVERN.apply at once when rotation is on
cast on|offcast.enabled only. It neither builds nor removes casts (see P4)

The verb is console-only. It is not in the controls registry or the web's verb whitelist (controls :724-728), and there is no cast row in the window.

6. Problems, gaps and suspicious logic (with lines)

P1. Under season casts, the FREQUENCY ladder and the apex scheduler are idle unless someone runs roster build.

  • castYear writes only allow and assign (:8617-8625). It never writes cfg.odds or roster.apex_keys.
  • ROSTER.placeTick returns at once with no apex keys and no invasives (:8896-8899).
  • ROSTER.build has exactly one caller, the verb (:18429). On a v7.3 fort, every species therefore runs at its raw FREQUENCY, and no apex is scheduled.
  • If roster build is run, its cfg.odds and apex_keys survive every later castYear. The apex scheduler then places only keys the cast wants this season (:8871). A cast apex that the build did not pick is never scheduled.
  • The registry's own help says this: "It acts only after roster build seats apexes" (controls :155).

P2. Stock writes are not undone by off, disable or all off.

  • disableSched (:15950-15981) and PANEL.restoreAll (:16042-16059) restore FREQUENCY, cluster, flags and raws, but never population quantities.
  • Every resting or out-of-season entry stays at quantity = 0, extinct = true. Its value is held in the RESERVE until the tool runs again.
  • Yet turn_off prints "every job stopped and every write put back" (:16275), and the PANEL comment says "puts back everything the tool wrote" (:15994).

P3. cast off does not survive a save and load.

  • castSanitize uses c.cast[k] = (type(r) == type(v)) and r or v (:8322). With a saved enabled = false, this gives true and false or true, which is true.
  • So after a reload the casts are on again, and they rebuild at the next new year.
  • The same trap would hit any future boolean in CAST_DEF that defaults to true.

P4. cast off does not bring back "the preset roster" as its help says (:18340).

  • It only clears cast.enabled (:18347-18350). allow and assign stay as the casts left them: this year's casts become a fixed, all-year roster, and resting species stay inactive.
  • cast on with no casts prints a hint, but castOn stays false until cast rebuild.

P5. restfreq 0 reaches past "resting cavern species".

  • CAVERN.apply applies restLevel to every held token while casts are on (:3753). That includes cast species out of their season, and deep keys.
  • PANEL.fortOn turns the deep layer on (the deep switch is not opt-in, :16011, :16101).
  • Under casts, deep species are made active with one default season by ROSTER.normalize in enableSched (:15933 — it runs whatever the casts say), because castManages never covers deep.
  • So with cast restfreq 0, magma-sea non-vermin species out of their one season are written FREQUENCY 0. The verb and its ledger line say "resting cavern species" (:18351-18357).

P6. The comment and commit on the vermin guard misstate the pool's vermin test.

  • 09ab266 and the comment at :3690-3691 say "the pool's vermin test reads only GROUNDER, ROTTER and SOIL".
  • classify actually reads six flags: GROUNDER, ROTTER, SOIL, FISH, EATER and SMALL_RACE (:1801-1802).
  • The added guard is harmless, but its stated reason is wrong.

P7. The sentient cast slot can never fill with the default settings.

  • ROSTER.slotOf returns SN or SNP only when roster.sn_slots is on (:7693), and that defaults to false (:7562).
  • Every cast's sentient slot therefore reports 0 of 1: none in season in the pool (:8531-8538). The real cast size is one less than the table's want.

P8. The cast and builder slot tables differ, and some guilds have no slot on some layers.

  • Water casts: no slot for GZ, PL or RP. A water-layer grazer, land prey or raptor is "no slot on this layer" and rests all year. LADDER22.water has GZ and PL weights (:7876), but SLOTS.water has no GZ or PL slot either.
  • Cavern: the builder has no GZ slot (:7746-7747), but the cavern cast seats GZ under "ground prey" (:8293).
  • Flying apex: recoded FAPX in the land cast (:8375). ROSTER.VDIET has no FAPX, so a flying apex in a land cast eats no vermin.

P9. The cast honours the raw NO_<season> flags, and the outcome depends on when the species was classified.

  • castPool drops a species whose raw forbids the season (:8394, :8406).
  • With seasons_own on (the default), the tool's season deal is meant to override the raws: ROSTER.fitSeason :2657; ENGINE.candidates :5999; exhaustCheck :3158. V7.apply clears those flags on managed raws (:13833-13835).
  • classify reads noSeason from the raw at first classification and memoizes it. After UNDO.after (:15985), extinct edits (:14381) or roster set ap_vermin_mass (:9267) clears CACHE.class while the flags are still cleared, noSeason reads all false. The same fort can then grow different casts.

P10. Cavern FREQUENCY writes are not restored at world unload.

  • The world-unload handler restores CURIOUS, V7, the trickle, sizes and HUNT (:17100-17106), but not CAVERN.restoreAll. Only disable and all off call it (:15953, :16045).
  • The CAVERN.restoreAll comment says it is "Called on disable, on unload" (:3656-3658). That is not true of the code.
  • The code relies on DF re-reading raws at load (:3619-3621). The snapshot stays in site data and is reused.

P11. cast rebuild is a full roster rewrite with no undo step (:18359-18369). roster build and the preset push one.

P12. Manual edits under casts are temporary, and some of them break the food web.

  • roster KEY active, seasons KEY ..., the window's "Re-apply preset" (gui :1544), the preset verb (:18273), roster build, and a newly enabled layer (layer verb :18292-18298; controls :806, which runs ROSTER.normalize) all write allow and assign while cfg.casts stays. The next new year's castYear overwrites them without warning.
  • The ecology keeps only cast edges (:5183). A species activated by hand, or by normalize, therefore gets no predator-prey relation writes.

P13. Exhaustion stand-ins under casts get no relation writes.

  • castReplaceOk admits a stand-in because it links to the cast (:8635-8661).
  • castEdgeSet holds only the edges grown into the cast (:8673-8684), so the stand-in's pairs are filtered out (:5183).

P14. The cast turnover may skip a run after a reload.

  • The comment says "Once per season (and once after load)" (:12775). But CACHE.castTurnStamp (:12781-12782) is not cleared by CACHE.drop (:17078-17096).
  • Reloading a save in the same year and season during one DFHack session skips the turnover. Only cast rebuild clears the stamp (:18365).

P15. The high-value memo is stale across settings and worlds.

  • CACHE.hv is keyed by token only, and nothing clears it (:8350-8368; it is not in CACHE.drop).
  • Changes to cast.hv_petvalue or cast.hv_mass, or a different world's raws in the same session, are ignored until DFHack restarts.

P16. The cast record is saved in full to site data on every saveConfig.

  • castYear stores each season's slots, log, edges, unfilled and excluded (one reason string per never-castable species) for 3 layers × 4 seasons (:8603-8605). castSanitize copies these back as is (:8336).
  • saveConfig writes the whole config (:1138) and is called from the groups pass, from exhaustion and from every edit. The code shows nothing that measures this cost.

P17. The web's "Build the roster" with "all" builds land only.

  • The action maps all to '' (controls :188, :905), so the verb runs as roster build.
  • layerArg = v or 'land' (:18424) then builds just land. There is no "every layer" path.

P18. Dead code.

  • No callers in the shipped scripts: ROSTER.effectiveMax (:7782), ROSTER.slotGuild (:7708).
  • Kept "for reference only": ROSTER.LADDER (:8686-8690).
  • Returns 0 but is still exported: fillThinSeasons (:2748, :17448).
  • Mentioned as "the vermin stream's entry point" but only the roster gobble verb calls it: ROSTER.gobbleEdgesActive (:8053). VERMIN.edges (:14607) falls back to the rule table when no build ran this session, so the casts' vermin edges never reach GOBBLE writes.

P19. Two knobs for one rule. Giants are weighted ×0.2 by roster.giant_pick in the builder (:7832) and by cast.giant in casts (:8477). Animal people use roster.ap_pick in both.

P20. Weak range checks.

  • roster set accepts any number ≥ 0 for numeric keys, and any numbers for pyramid (:9249-9260). The load sanitiser bounds them later (0..1e7; pyramid 0..100).
  • castSanitize takes any cavern_rest_freq number (:8324). A negative value falls into the 0 path of restLevel.

P21. The cavern gate's hold can bump a FREQUENCY-0 resting species back to 1.

  • V7.GRP.holdFor (:12691-12699) knows nothing of restLevel. When a cavern reaches its cap, cavernHold writes 1 (CAVERN.SUPPRESSED) for species not wanted this season (:12752-12757).
  • With restfreq 0, those stay at 1 until the next daily CAVERN.apply.

P22. Casts are never built on forts enabled before v7.3 (full_enable_roster already true, :16090). Those forts keep their preset or builder roster until cast rebuild, with no notice.

P23. No offline test covers the casts. tests/ holds aquarium, gui, perf, rig, water and web. None of them names castYear, castGrow or cast rebuild.

M2Seasonal rotation and arrival control

The daily job arms a timer for the exact season-change tick; the change gives back borrowed seasons, regrows casts at a new year, zeroes the out-of-season entries into the reserve, refills the in-season ones, and resets cavern frequencies. Between changes the groups pass (every 300 ticks) re-pins the holds, releases DF's gated waves on an adaptive clock, trims caverns and sends off off-cast groups once per season.

The jobs

  • Groups pass, every 300 ticks: re-pin holds, discovery and adoption, the release clock, the cavern gate and trim, the cast turnover, the exhaustion check.
  • Daily: the season timer, cavern FREQUENCY, the spill (off under casts), the apex scheduler, a registry rescan.
  • Ecology, every 3,000 ticks: the relation writes (M3). Scavenging every 200, curious thieves every 50, quiet fights every 10.
  • All are DFHack repeat timers behind fuses; the C++ plugin only bridges autostart and map load and schedules none of this.

One season change, in tick order

  1. The timer fires at the boundary (retrying 10-120 ticks until DF's own season turns).
  2. V7.ST.turn: spill borrows given back; at Winter → Spring the year's casts regrow; applyLive zeroes out-of-season entries into the reserve (extinct set) and refills in-season ones from it; CACHE.appliedStamp is set.
  3. CAVERN.apply: resting cavern species to restfreq, vermin always 1.
  4. Next groups pass: castTurnover zeroes the leave countdown of every tracked group whose species left the cast (water groups via their land key); DF walks them off. Nothing is teleported.
  5. The exhaustion check, now waiting for the apply's stamp, hands an empty cast niche to a stand-in.

The caps

Land and each water body type: floor(√embark tiles) + 1 groups, or one fixed cap. Caverns: 5 each. DF decides when a wave comes; the tool can only withhold the release of a gated wave (land, caverns) or draw a group itself (water). That asymmetry is why land overshoots slightly and caverns a lot.

Most consequential findings. The cavern trim counts groups already sent off at the turnover and so trims the new cast for days (P3, a bug with a one-line fix). The turnover runs once per season, so an off-cast group arriving after it stays all season (P4). The reserve is discarded when a DF refund lands just before the apply (P6). An error in the season turn stops rotation for the season, because the daily job calls it without a guard (P8). Disable leaves the world held (P9). enable turns on the deep layer against R60 (P15). Air-breathing "semiaquatic" species are placed on the deepest water tile and drown, and the mix then boosts them (P5).

Full code notes: rotation and arrivals (mech/rotation.md)

Source: /Users/nathanielcannon/Claude/Projects/sw-wt/plugin, branch v7.2-plugin, HEAD 8185d85 (clean). Read from the code only. Nothing was run against the game.

Where a doc disagrees with the code, the code wins, and the disagreement is listed in section 10.

0. The model in one page

Two drivers. Every layer gets its animals through one of two drivers.

  • Driver A: DF draws. This covers land, sea life listed on land entries, and caverns 1-3. DF sends a "wave" from a population source whenever no flagged animal of that source is on the map. A source is a region tile x feature x cave x population entry; see srcKey at sw:4307 and the gate notes at sw:4167-4187 and sw:12567-12575. The tool steers these draws three ways:
    • Who comes:
      • on the surface, by the regional entry's quantity and flags.extinct (applyLive sw:3027, holdOutOfSeason sw:3072);
      • in the caverns, by the creature raw's frequency (CAVERN.apply sw:3698). Entry quantity gates nothing underground (sw:3548-3557, sw:3614-3621).
    • When: by holding DF's own gate shut. A wave's animals keep the roaming_wilderness_population_source flag, and the tool clears that flag (a "release") only on its own clock (releaseGroup sw:4411, detachOldest sw:4424).
    • How many at once: by a per-layer group cap (QUOTA.groupsFor sw:3526). In the caverns there is also a frequency hold and a trim (V7.GRP.cavernPass sw:12591).
  • Driver B: the tool draws. This covers water bodies (ocean, lake, river or brook, pool), because DF never waves a feature entry in play (sw:4583-4586). The tool picks a species (ENGINE.candidates sw:5972, V7.WAT.mix sw:6394). It creates the animals with dfhack.units.create (PLACE.one sw:4821), debits the entry one per animal (sw:6125), and tracks them as a group under a per-body-type cap and clock (V7.waterTick sw:9280).

The roster is the season. Every managed key has an explicit cfg.allow[key] (true = active, false = inactive) and, when active, cfg.assign[key] = a list of seasons 0-3. ROSTER.wants(cfg, key, season) is the single test every pass uses: allow == true and the season is in assign (sw:2726). Keys:

  • land species are keyed TOKEN;
  • other layers are keyed water:TOKEN, cavern:TOKEN or deep:TOKEN (keyFor sw:1411).

The layer comes from the entry: cave_id gives cavern (depth 0-2) or deep (3+), feature_idx gives water, anything else is land (layerOf sw:1403).

v7.3 season casts. When cfg.cast.enabled and cfg.casts exist (ROSTER.castOn sw:8305), the roster is generated once a year:

  • For each layer (land, water, cavern) and each season, a "cast" is grown from a high-value seed through its prey and predators into fixed guild slots (ROSTER.castGrow sw:8451, slots sw:8282-8297).
  • A species in some season's cast is active with exactly those seasons.
  • Every other species the cast layer manages "rests" (allow = false, no seasons).
  • Locked species that would rest go into cfg.casts.rest (ROSTER.castYear sw:8589-8631; ROSTER.managedKey sw:2723).

1. The job schedule

1.1 Registration

All recurring jobs are DFHack repeat-util repeats (sw:518). Each is wrapped by FUSE.job (sw:4233) and started through V7.PERF.every (sw:16466).

  • V7.PERF.every starts each repeat behind a one-shot dfhack.timeout(phase, 'ticks'), registered in repeat-util's own table so repeatUtil.cancel(name) also cancels the pending start (sw:16460-16479). With perf.stagger off, or no map loaded, it calls scheduleEvery directly.
  • Phases are fixed offsets from the enable tick: V7.PERF.PHASE = { groups = 31, daily = 77, ecology = 150, scav = 37, alerts = 5, curious = 23, forage = 61 } (sw:16465).
  • Jobs are scheduled from enableSched (sw:15926-15949) and scheduleGroups (sw:13330-13335). Both run on enable rotation, on PANEL.fortOn (enable/on), and at every map load of an enabled fort (PANEL.onMapLoad sw:16214).

What does not use repeat-util:

  • The season timer (V7.ST, v7.3): a bare dfhack.timeout armed by the daily job (sw:4124-4128). It is not FUSE-timed.
  • The split-off water pass: a bare dfhack.timeout(3) (V7.PASS.waterLater sw:13164-13174), run under the groups job's FUSE name.
  • Sliced load-time surveys: per-tick dfhack.timeout(1,'ticks') coroutine steps (V7.PERF.slice sw:16790-16811). While paused they use per-frame steps (V7.PERF.drivePaused sw:16846-16862). The sliced work is the caverns, the wet edge, the water tiles, vegetation and the water-body registry scan (V7.PERF.warm sw:16863-16873).
  • FUSE defers: a 1-tick dfhack.timeout re-run when another heavy job already used this tick, at most 3 times (FUSE.DEFER sw:4232, sw:4237-4247).
  • eventful: used only to feed the census's wild-unit id set (onUnitNewActive, V7.PERF.eventsOn sw:16568-16583). It schedules no rotation work.
  • The C++ plugin: schedules no rotation work. It only:
    • calls the Lua module at SC_CORE_INITIALIZED (autostart, cpp:7481-7490);
    • sets bridge_pending at SC_MAP_LOADED when the plugin is enabled (cpp:7491-7492), and calls on_map_loaded on the next frame (cpp:7430-7436 → plua:91-94 → map_loaded sw:16280);
    • turns the renderer on or off (plugin_enable cpp:7410-7422 → turn_on/turn_off sw:16219/16257).
    • wscan (cpp:6938-6981) is the native water-body scan the registry can use (V7.WB.native). It is a classifier, not a scheduler.
  • The engine's own state hook: dfhack.onStateChange[MODULE] (sw:17098-17115).
    • On SC_MAP_LOADED and SC_WORLD_UNLOADED it runs CACHE.drop.
    • On world unload it also restores every raw write (each in its own pcall), cancels every job and sets lastSeason = nil.
    • On map load it runs PANEL.onMapLoad.

What the daily job does, in order:

  1. A season change if cur_season ~= lastSeason (V7.ST.turn). Otherwise holdOutOfSeason, then CAVERN.apply.
  2. V7.ST.arm (sets the season timer).
  3. V7.WB.daily: rescans the water-body registry at a new season, a newly found cavern or a settings change.
  4. ROSTER.placeTick: the apex scheduler, at most once a game day.

Budgets and fuses (FUSE sw:4202):

  • Every job pass is timed. Over JOB_MS (250 ms) it prints a warning. Over TRIP_MS (2,000 ms), or on any Lua error, FUSE.trip cancels the repeat outright, logs a fuse ledger line and keeps the trip in site data until enable re-arms (sw:4208-4216, sw:4273-4277).
  • BUDGET_MS (50) only counts passes "over".
  • Heavy scans take a SCAN_MS (1,500) deadline.
  • Each pass shares one unit census (CACHE.census), opened and closed by FUSE.job (sw:4251-4256).
  • Each job's parts are timed into the same stats by FUSE.lap (sw:4287).

Coincidence. With the default cadences the phases never land on the same tick (checked by modular arithmetic: groups ≡31 mod 300, daily ≡77 mod 1200, ecology ≡150 mod 3000, scav ≡37 mod 200, curious ≡23 mod 50, alerts ≡5 mod 10, forage ≡61 mod 100, the water pass ≡34 mod 300). If two jobs do meet (after a player cadence change or a defer), the later heavy one waits a tick (sw:4229-4247). The season timer can fire on any tick, and nothing staggers it.

1.3 Order inside one groups pass (groupsTick, sw:13188-13305)
  1. holdOutOfSeason (every 300 t since v6.3, sw:13190-13194)
  2. Waits if the load-time survey is still slicing (returns early, at most WAIT_PASSES = 20 passes, sw:13202-13206, sw:16834-16841)
  3. A private config copy if a job-path config writer has work (V7.PERF.writersDue sw:16490-16510)
  4. v7.3 season-change fallback: if lastSeason ~= nil and cur_season ~= lastSeason, it cancels the timer and runs V7.ST.turn (in a pcall), then re-reads the config (sw:13210-13218)
  5. ROSTER.exhaustCheck (sw:13219)
  6. V7.WAT.spillCheck (once a game day; returns at once under casts, sw:7362)
  7. reconcileGroups drops members that have gone; a finished group's stay feeds the clock's W (sw:4370-4386, V7.GRP.observe sw:12371)
  8. PATTERN.trickleApply, V7.GRP.apCap, PATTERN.sizeApply, PATTERN.dawnStanding
  9. discoverGroups: new flagged waves become gated groups and get an arrive ledger line (sw:4388-4407, sw:13229-13230)
  10. V7.GRP.adoptNatives (every 1,200 t, sw:12800)
  11. V7.GRP.castTurnover (once per season stamp, sw:12778)
  12. applyCohesion (leaders and panic) and stuckSweep
  13. Coupling or pattern-table end/start (coupling is parked)
  14. The Driver B water step (deferred +3 t inside a scheduled pass), then sponges
  15. The land release (sw:13268-13288)
  16. V7.GRP.cavernPass: cavern release, hold and trim (sw:13291-13296)
  17. IRRUPT.tick (sw:13300)
  18. saveGroups

2. The season deal

2.1 Who gets which season
  • Without casts (the preset, matrix or manual roster), seasons come from ROSTER.deal (sw:2665-2673). Species are sorted by climate lean within their group (realm|habitat|role, sw:2638-2640) and dealt one season each by quarter (ROSTER.quarterOf sw:2647, order Winter, Autumn, Spring, Summer = ROSTER.ORDER {3,2,0,1} sw:2631).
  • ROSTER.normalize (sw:2699-2714) makes the roster whole: every in-embark, unlocked species gets an explicit allow; an active one with no season gets one by ROSTER.defaultSeason (sw:2675); an inactive one is cleared of seasons. It runs at every enableSched, so at every load (sw:15933).
  • With casts, ROSTER.castYear (sw:8589) writes allow and assign for every pool entry a cast layer manages (ROSTER.castManages sw:8576-8586). Casts are reseeded per site, year, season and layer:
    • seed = (site*7919 + year*104729 + s*131 + #layer*17 + salt) % 2^31-1 (sw:8602);
    • a species in last winter's cast is weighted carry 0.25 (sw:8475), so the casts turn over year to year.
2.2 DF's NO_SPRING / NO_SUMMER / NO_AUTUMN / NO_WINTER versus seasons_own
  • DF honours NO_<season> at its own pick (ECO T2, cited at sw:2650-2653). classify records them per creature as noSeason[0..3] (sw:1822-1823). Classification is memoized per world in CACHE.class (sw:1796).
  • v7.seasons_own defaults to on (sw:840), and V7.grpSanitize forces it on at migration (sw:728). With it on:
    • ROSTER.fitSeason returns the dealt season unchanged (sw:2657-2663);
    • V7.apply clears every NO_<season> caste flag on every in-embark, unlocked species in the pool, recorded through V7.rec (sw:13833-13835);
    • the flags come back on disable, All off and world unload (V7.restore sw:13741, sw:15966, sw:16051, sw:17102);
    • Driver B ignores noSeason too (sw:5995-5999).
  • With it off, the deal moves a forbidden season to the next allowed one (sw:2661) and Driver B skips the species in that season.
  • Casts honour the raws whatever seasons_own says. ROSTER.castPool drops a species with noSeason[season] (sw:8393, sw:8406), and ROSTER.castReplaceOk refuses one as a stand-in (sw:8650). The flags are read from the memoized classification, so this holds only if CACHE.class was built before V7.apply cleared them (section 9, item P10).
2.3 What a season change does (V7.ST.turn, sw:4093-4109)

Called once per change by whichever comes first: the timer (V7.ST.now), the groups-pass fallback, or the daily job.

  1. lastSeason = s (first, before any work).
  2. Copy-on-write of the shared config (sw:4095).
  3. ROSTER.exhaustRoll: borrowed seasons given back, exhausted marks forgotten (sw:3106-3120).
  4. V7.WAT.spillRoll: water spill borrows given back (sw:7342-7358).
  5. If casts are on and casts.year ~= cur_year: ROSTER.castYear grows this year's casts and saves (sw:4098-4101). In practice this happens at Winter → Spring, or at the first apply after a load into a later year.
  6. applyLive(cfg, s) (sw:3027-3063):
    • For every managed entry on an enabled layer:
      • In season (ROSTER.wants):
        • a player stock (cfg.stock[key]) is written exactly, spread over the entries (RESERVE.set sw:3015), unless the key is exhausted;
        • an entry at quantity ≤ 0 is refilled from the reserve res[i], else the worldgen snapshot default_snapshot[key], else qtyFor = in_season_qty × weight / 50 = 100 by default (sw:2453, sw:3042-3048);
        • an entry above 0 is left as DF keeps it;
        • the reserve slot is then cleared and extinct = (quantity <= 0) (sw:3049-3050).
      • Out of season, inactive or resting: the quantity is saved into the reserve and the entry is set to quantity = 0, extinct = true, "both barriers" (sw:3053-3054).
    • It sets **CACHE.appliedStamp = year*4 + season** when season == cur_season (sw:3061).
  7. A DF announcement "<Season> wildlife roster applied." (sw:4103) and a season ledger line "<Season> roster applied: land 9+3 (seed …), …" (sw:4104).
  8. PATTERN.trickleApply (sw:4105).
  9. CAVERN.apply(cfg, s): cavern and deep FREQUENCY for the new season (sw:4107, section 3.4).

Nothing in the turn dismisses groups or rescans water. The turnover runs in the next groups pass (castTurnover), and the registry rescan in the next daily pass (V7.WB.daily sw:6851-6864).

2.4 The v7.3 season timer (commit 34a3a4b)
  • V7.ST.arm is called by every daily pass. When the boundary is ≤ 1,500 t away (V7.ST.TICKS = 403,200/4 = 100,800), it arms a one-shot timeout for the boundary tick (sw:4124-4128). The daily cadence is 1,200 t, so the last day before a change always arms it.
  • V7.ST.now (sw:4111-4123):
    • It returns if the tool is off or lastSeason == nil (no apply yet since the load).
    • If DF has not turned cur_season yet, it re-arms every 10 t, up to 12 tries (120 t).
    • Otherwise it runs pcall(V7.ST.turn). An error becomes a fuse ledger line.
  • Fallback: the groups pass (sw:13210-13218), then the daily job.
  • V7.ST.cancel runs in enableSched (sw:15938), disableSched (sw:15951) and the groups fallback.
  • CACHE.drop forgets the timer id (sw:17092), because tick timeouts die with the map.
2.5 CACHE.appliedStamp and the exhaustion race (commit 6e1ffb2)
  • ROSTER.exhaustCheck returns at once unless CACHE.appliedStamp == year*4 + cur_season (sw:3128).
  • Before the fix, the groups pass could reach a boundary before the daily apply. It found the new season's species still at 0 from their rest, called them exhausted, and swapped 17 of 22 autumn cast species for stand-ins (the comment at sw:3124-3127).
  • The stamp is set only by applyLive (sw:3061) and dropped with the map (sw:17091). So after a load no exhaustion check runs until the first daily pass (+77 t) has applied the season.

3. Holding and resting: keeping out-of-cast species away

3.1 Surface (land and water entries): quantity, extinct flag, reserve
MechanismWhereWhat
Season applyapplyLive sw:3027Out of season: res[i] = quantity, then quantity = 0, extinct = true. In season: refill only entries at 0.
HoldholdOutOfSeason sw:3072-3090Every managed entry with quantity > 0 that the roster does not want this season is pinned back to 0 and extinct, and the amount is added to its reserve. Runs every groups pass (sw:13194) and every daily pass (sw:4141).
Why the hold re-runssw:3065-3071, sw:13190-13192DF refunds a departing animal to the entry it came from, whether or not it still has its flag (E15, v5.3, sw:4181-4187). A refund to an out-of-season entry would let DF draw a fresh out-of-season wave.
Reserve storeRESERVE sw:2974-3012Site-data key seasonal-wildlife/reserve, keyed by position in world.populations.all (tostring(r.i)). RESERVE.of reports live and held stock.
Player stockcfg.stock[key], RESERVE.set sw:3015Written exactly at the apply. A stock of 0 is "a choice, not exhaustion" (sw:3098-3099, sw:3132).

How stock comes back in season. At the next applyLive with the species in season, each entry at quantity ≤ 0 takes back its remembered reserve (or the snapshot, or 100) and its extinct flag is cleared. DF then debits one per arriving animal and breeds the entry up (sw:3069-3070). Driver B debits one per placed animal (sw:6125). A stand-in or spill restocks the same way (sw:3173-3183, sw:7404-7413).

3.2 Caverns (and deep): raw FREQUENCY
  • CAVERN.apply (sw:3698-3760) runs at every season change and every daily pass. It builds a want per raw token from every key on the cavern layer (when layers.cavern is on), the deep layer (layers.deep), or any key with player odds.
    • Open (wanted this season by any key of the token): the player's odds, or the raw restored from the snapshot (floored by the R61 animal-people floor, sw:3742).
    • Held (a cavern or deep key not wanted, or passed over by a call): CAVERN.SUPPRESSED = 1 (sw:3630).
    • Under casts, held species take CAVERN.restLevel instead (sw:3753): cfg.cast.cavern_rest_freq (default 1; cast restfreq 0|1 sw:18351-18357).
  • restfreq 0 vermin guard (09ab266, sw:3683-3697): FREQUENCY 0 is allowed only when the raw is not vermin by classify and carries none of VERMIN_FISH, VERMIN_SOIL_COLONY, VERMIN_ROTTER, VERMIN_GROUNDER, VERMIN_SOIL, nor the caste flag VERMIN_MICRO. Otherwise it stays at 1. The reason is in the comments: CREEPY_CRAWLER at 0 froze DF (sw:3623-3629); FREQUENCY 1 "still leaks ~15%" (sw:3681).
  • Locked species a cast rests (casts.rest: BLOOD_MAN, ELEMENTMAN_MUD…) are held too, though they have no allow entry (sw:3716-3723).
  • Land keys are never held by raw (sw:3678): "A land key out of season is held by its stock, not by its raw."
  • Snapshot: every value written is first kept in seasonal-wildlife/cavern site data (CAVERN.write sw:3647-3654; CAVERN.saved/save sw:3640-3644). It is put back by CAVERN.restoreAll (sw:3659-3668) on disable, All off and unload. An orphan sweep restores holds no layer or gate owns any more (V7.GRP.orphans sw:12708-12722).
3.3 The hold is re-asserted in the groups job
  • Every 300 t: holdOutOfSeason (sw:13194).
  • Daily: holdOutOfSeason and CAVERN.apply (sw:4141-4142).
  • The cavern gate's own frequency hold changes whenever its at-cap set changes (V7.GRP.cavernHold sw:12723-12768, keyed by CACHE.capSig).
  • Not every 300 t: CAVERN.apply. A cavern raw changed by something else stays changed until the next daily pass. Examples: a stand-in promoted in a cavern, or a gate hold written over a resting species (section 9, P7).

4. Exhaustion and stand-ins

ROSTER.exhaustCheck (sw:3121-3193) runs every groups pass, after the apply stamp check.

  1. exhaustRoll (same stamp: no-op).
  2. For every key wanted this season (and not stock 0, not already done), sum the entries' live quantity. Every key at 0 is exhausted: x.done[key] = true.
  3. For each exhausted non-vermin key, it picks a stand-in:
    • Without casts: the same ROSTER.group (realm|habitat|role). The score is the log-mass distance, plus 100 when the guild differs.
    • With casts: ROSTER.castReplaceOk (sw:8635-8662). The stand-in must fill the same cast slot on the same layer and eat, or be eaten by, a member of this season's cast. A resting species may be chosen (cfg.allow == false is accepted under casts, sw:3155).
    • In both cases the stand-in must:
      • not be in season already;
      • not be done or promoted;
      • have live + reserve + snapshot stock > 0;
      • without seasons_own, not be forbidden that season by the raws.
  4. The stand-in gets the season added to its assign and allow = true. Its entries are restocked from reserve, snapshot or qtyFor, and extinct is cleared. It is recorded in x.promoted[key] = { season, for_key, resting } with an edit ledger line (sw:3167-3185).
  5. While x.done holds a key, applyLive does not refill it (ROSTER.exhaustHolds sw:3101-3104, sw:3041-3042).

Retirement (ROSTER.exhaustRoll sw:3106-3120, at the season change or at the first check of a new stamp):

  • The borrowed season is removed from each stand-in's assign, but never when that would leave an active species seasonless.
  • A stand-in that was resting goes back to rest (allow = false, assign nil, sw:3114).
  • done and promoted are cleared.
  • The stand-in's entries are then zeroed by the turn's applyLive, because it is no longer in season.
  • Its groups already on the map:
    • Under casts, the next castTurnover dismisses them (no longer wanted).
    • Without casts they stay until their own leave countdowns run out.

Caverns: a cavern stand-in's stock is opened at once, but its FREQUENCY stays held until the next daily CAVERN.apply, up to one game day later (exhaustCheck does not call CAVERN.apply).

5. Turnover at a season change, and natives

5.1 V7.GRP.castTurnover (sw:12778-12799), casts only
  • Once per year*4 + season stamp, kept in CACHE.castTurnStamp. Only cast rebuild clears it (sw:18365).
  • It walks every tracked group that is not already dismissed and not an irruption wave. It computes the key from the group's layer:
    • keyFor(layer, token) first;
    • fix 8817eb4 (sw:12788-12791): if that key is not managed but the plain land key is, it uses the land key. Ocean life and river fish have no feature index, so the pool files them under their land key even when Driver B drew them into water groups.
  • A group whose key is managed and not wanted this season is dismissed (dismissGroup), with one ledger line listing the species.
5.2 How send-off works mechanically
PathWritesTeleport?Lines
dismissGroup (turnover, groups dismiss)every live member animal.leave_countdown = 0; follower links cleared; grp.dismissed = true; roaming flags left as they arenosw:10594-10601
ENGINE.sendOff (`sendoff landcavern, a call`, the window's Ctrl+F)discover first, then for every gated group of the layer: dismissGroup + releaseGroup (both roaming flags cleared); resets that layer's release clock to nownosw:10613-10630
V7.GRP.trimOne (cavern over cap)each natural member's leave_countdown = 10 (the old value kept in g.trim_undo and put back on disable, All off and unload if the unit is still there); trimmed, dismissed, and trim_gated for a DF wavenosw:12636-12673, sw:13055-13067
holdGroupraises countdownsnosw:10584-10593

The animals walk off on DF's own leave path. Nothing teleports, kills or deletes them. A dismissed group stays in g.groups, and in every count, until reconcileGroups sees its members gone (sw:4361-4386). For a group in an enclosed lake or pool, no code checks that a path off the map exists.

5.3 Discovery of DF waves vs adoption of natives
  • Discovery (discoverGroups sw:4388-4407, gatedLayer sw:4351-4359) counts any active, living, non-invader unit carrying flags2.roaming_wilderness_population_source with feature_idx == -1. A unit with no cave is land; a cave of depth 0-2 is cavern. Units are grouped by race|source into one gated group (resident = false).
  • Adoption (V7.GRP.adoptNatives sw:12800-12854, every ADOPT_EVERY = 1,200 t; CACHE.grpAdoptAt) takes any natural wild unit that no record holds and that carries no roaming flag:
    • a young one whose mother is tracked joins her group;
    • otherwise it is grouped by layer|race|source as a native (land or cavern; counted) or a seeded water school (led, never counted).
  • Defaults outside casts: natives_cavern = true, natives_land = false, seeded_water = true (sw:802).
  • Under casts (v7.3, sw:12809-12822):
    • every land native is adopted, whatever natives_land says;
    • every water unit is adopted;
    • a unit flagged in a water feature (DF's embark fish) is adopted too; otherwise discovery and adoption both skip it.
    • Adopted natives of resting species are then dismissed by the same pass's castTurnover. Adoption runs before turnover in the pass.

Natives at load. At map load:

  1. The first groups pass (+31 t) holds stock and, if the load-time survey has finished, adopts and turns over.
  2. No exhaustion runs and the season apply has not happened (lastSeason nil) until the daily pass at +77 t. That pass makes a full V7.ST.turn, with the announcement, at every load.

6. Group caps and the gate

6.1 Caps (QUOTA.groupsFor sw:3526-3537)
Layer keyCapDefault
landlimits.mode == 'formula': floor(sqrt(embark tiles)) + 1, where embark tiles = (map.x_count//48) * (map.y_count//48) (QUOTA.autoGroups sw:3508-3513); 'fixed': limits.fixedformula, so 2 on a 1x1, 5 on a 4x4, 9 on an 8x8
water:<ocean|lake|river|pool>the same formula or fixed value, per body type, not per individual body (V7.GRP.lk sw:12320-12325; waterTick counts grp.body == body sw:9294)as land
cavern:<0|1|2>groups.cavern_cap, universal; under fixed mode min(cavern_cap, fixed)5
deepno key, no cap (R60)—

Animal ceilings (limits.<layer>.ceiling, default 0 = none) are separate:

  • land: no release at or over the ceiling (sw:13272-13273);
  • water: no draw at or over it (sw:9306-9307);
  • cavern: every cavern species held at 1 by CAVERN.apply while over (sw:3726-3734).

QUOTA.cavernThrottle (sw:3574-3609) has no caller and QUOTA.cavern returns 0 (sw:3558), so it is dead code.

6.2 The release clock (R31, V7.GRP.ctl/gapFor/dueTick/releaseGap sw:12344-12421)

Each layer key keeps its own controller. Its state lives in g.ctl[lk] in the groups record.

  • W, the mean stay, is an exponential mean (w_alpha 0.2) of finished groups' stays. Priors: land 34,500, water 27,000, cavern 30,000. Natives, seeded, trimmed and irruption groups do not feed it (sw:12372).
  • L* is redrawn uniformly in [cap - target_band, cap] (band 1) at every release, with a jitter 1 ± gap_jitter (0.35).
  • gap = W / L* × f × jitter, where:
    • d = L* - n (n = groups there now);
    • f = 1/(1 + catchup×d) when d > 0, else 1 + catchup×|d|;
    • the result is clamped to [gap_floor_days, gap_max_days] = [0.5, 20] days.
  • Each pass recomputes the due tick from the last release with the current n. The layer's timer only ever moves earlier. At n ≥ cap the clock returns nil, which pauses it.
  • adaptive off, or the burst pattern, uses PATTERN.nextGap: 5-20 jitter days (gap_min_days, gap_max_days), or burst gaps (sw:10236-10254).

Land release (sw:13268-13288). All of these must hold:

  • no coupling or pattern table restored this pass;
  • nLand < cap, where nLand = ENGINE.count(g,'land'), every land group except seeded (sw:6147-6151), so natives, placed apex groups and dismissed groups that have not left all count;
  • now ≥ g.next_wave_tick;
  • under the land ceiling.

Then detachOldest releases the oldest gated land group (sw:4424-4434), and its source can draw again.

gate_drain (v7.gate_drain, on): V7.drainGate (sw:4445-4464) then releases the next-oldest gated groups of the layer until at most one flagged animal remains. It releases at most room = cap - n - 1 extras (sw:13282).

6.3 The cavern gate (R44, V7.GRP.cavernPass sw:12591-12635)

Per depth d, with cap = cavern_cap (5):

  • Count: every cavern group of depth d except running irruption waves: DF waves (gated and released), natives, placed and adopted groups, and dismissed or trimmed groups not yet gone (sw:12595-12601).
  • Release: if a gated group exists and n < cap and the depth's clock is due, detachOldest(g,'cavern',d). The gap is multiplied by 0.5 while irruption pressure for that cavern is high (IRRUPT.gapDays sw:10938-10953, sw:12607, sw:12615), then gate_drain runs.
  • Trim (cavern_trim, on; trim_days 1): if n > cap, at most one group per depth per day (V7.GRP.trimOne sw:12636-12673):
    • the oldest native first, else the oldest resident;
    • with cavern_trim_gated (on, ruled 2 Oct) and no resident left, the oldest gated DF wave. Its source then reopens (sw:12649-12652).
  • Hold (V7.GRP.cavernHold sw:12723-12768): while any cavern a species lives in is at cap (cavern_hold = 'any'), every natural species with an Animal entry in a cavern and none on the surface or below the caverns (V7.GRP.species sw:12529-12559; cavern_hold_shared off) is held:
    • at V7.GRP.holdLevel = max(2, weight // 10), never above its weight (cavern_hold_mix on, sw:12683-12688);
    • at 1 if the roster itself holds it (V7.GRP.holdFor sw:12691-12700).
    • It releases only the holds it made itself (CACHE.capOwn) and then re-runs CAVERN.apply so the roster's own holds stand (sw:12738-12762).
  • The cavern gate at 5: the hard part is release withholding. It only stops a source that currently has a flagged (gated) group on the map (comment sw:12571-12573, sw:12580).
6.4 Water caps and the tool's own draws (V7.waterTick sw:9280-9345)

For each body type the registry holds:

  1. n = water groups of that type that are not seeded; cap = QUOTA.groupsFor('water:<type>').
  2. The adaptive due tick, but never inside an empty-draw back-off (g.water_retry, sw:9297-9301).
  3. A scheduled pass tries at most one body (V7.PASS.WATER_BODIES).
  4. ENGINE.draw (sw:6081-6103):
    • candidates: active, in season, stocked managed entries on the water layer, or AQUATIC land entries when water.land_aquatic is on (sw:5972-6014);
    • a body type the species may enter (V7.WB.fitting sw:6942-6956; brooks take adult mass ≤ 10,000 cm³ only, sw:6918-6941);
    • weighted by ENGINE.weight × V7.WAT.mix;
    • up to 3 species tried (V7.WAT.RETRIES).
  5. ENGINE.drawOne (sw:6104-6146):
    • group size from cfg.group_size or the raw cluster;
    • capped by stock and ceiling room;
    • the entry tile from V7.WAT.entry (sw:7151): an edge column for oceans and rivers, else edge, then nearest the centroid; the column tile is the first full (7/7) tile from the bottom up (V7.WAT.colTile sw:7043-7054; runs encode zz = bottom*1024 + top, sw:6542-6548);
    • the group fills outward through breathable tiles of the same body (sw:7092-7120);
    • each unit is placed by PLACE.one (create, copy the six-field population reference, leave countdown water.countdown 25,000 ± 20%, clear the roaming flags, set position, insert into units.active, occupancy bit, enemy slot; sw:4821-4846);
    • the entry is debited by 1 per unit;
    • the group record has drawn = true, resident = true (never gated);
    • it is led in the same pass (sw:9332).
  6. After a draw the next one waits on the adaptive gap. After an empty draw it waits exactly water.retry_days (1).

Cavern pools are never drawn by Driver B: V7.GRP.BODIES is ocean, lake, river and pool only (sw:695).

6.5 Season spill (thin water bodies; V7.WAT.spillCheck sw:7359-7423)
  • Once a game day.
  • For each body type with fewer than water.spill.min (3) drawable in-season candidates, active out-of-season water species (nearest dealt season first) borrow the current season. Their entries are restocked from reserve, snapshot or qtyFor.
  • The borrow is recorded in water.spill_state.borrowed, given back at the change (spillRoll in V7.ST.turn), on disable (sw:15972) and on water spill off.
  • Under casts the spill is off (return 0, sw:7362): "the water cast is the season's water roster."
6.6 Irruption and the gate

Irruption (opt-in; irruption.enabled defaults to false, sw:10754, but enable/PANEL.fortOn turns every non-parked Panel switch on, including irruption, sw:16102):

  • halves the cavern's release gap while pressure is ≥ gap_share × threshold or the layer is in warning or active (sw:10938-10953, sw:12607);
  • its waves are tool-placed, outside the cavern cap and never trimmed or turned over while the event runs (sw:12597, sw:12639, sw:12785);
  • lifts the animal-people cluster cap on that cavern (sw:13001-13003).
  • When the event ends, grp.irruption is cleared (sw:11796). The survivors then count against the cap and can be trimmed.

b0895b9. Until this commit, saveConfig wrote cast and casts but loadConfigRaw never read them back. After any save and load a fort ran with no casts and the cast switch off, and full_enable_roster and migrated_v71 were lost the same way (comment sw:8306-8309). V7.castSanitize (sw:8315-8347), called last in loadConfigRaw (sw:1058), now reads back:

  • cast (only the CAST_DEF keys plus cavern_rest_freq);
  • casts.year, casts.built, the per-layer per-season records (members, vermin, seed and the rest copied as written), and casts.rest;
  • full_enable_roster and migrated_v71.

cfg.cast is not in defaultConfig; ROSTER.castCfg creates it on demand with enabled = true (sw:8298-8304).

Raw writes are memory only. This covers NO_<season> clears, FREQUENCY, cluster sizes (trickle, group size, animal-people cap), hunting flags and the rest. DF re-reads raws on load. Population quantities, extinct flags and units' leave countdowns are saved in the world.

7.2 Map load
  1. CACHE.drop (sw:17078-17097) clears:
    • cfg, ledger, pops index, reserve cache, cavern snapshot cache, groups cache (PERF.drop), census, surveys, water-body registry;
    • appliedStamp, boundaryTimer, waterLater;
    • per world only: class memos, race indices, cave depths.
  2. PANEL.onMapLoad (sw:16214): if cfg.enabled, enableSched (sw:15926-15949) runs:
    • V7.WAT.autoLayer (water layer on if the map has water and the player never set it, sw:7311-7326);
    • buildPool, ROSTER.normalize, CACHE.managedPops();
    • HUNT.apply, CURIOUS.apply, V7.apply (NO_<season> cleared again, etc.);
    • saveConfig, lastSeason = nil, V7.ST.cancel, FUSE.reset;
    • V7.PERF.warm (sliced surveys and the registry scan);
    • every job scheduled.
    • It also runs IRRUPT.MASK.onLoad.
  3. The plugin's bridge (when the renderer is enabled) calls map_loaded on the next frame (sw:16280-16291):
    • a fort with no config at all gets PANEL.fortOn (everything on; casts grown when cast.enabled; sw:16086-16124);
    • otherwise it runs onMapLoad only if the engine's own handler missed the load.
  4. In the first ticks:
    • +31: groups pass (hold; wait for the survey, or adopt and turn over);
    • +77: the daily pass makes the full season turn (applyLive, CAVERN.apply, appliedStamp). With casts, castYear runs if the save's casts.year is older than the current year.
7.3 Disable, All off, unload
  • disable / disableSched (sw:15950-15978):
    • cancels the timer;
    • restores cavern FREQUENCY (CAVERN.restoreAll), trickle, group size (which reaches V7.GRP.restoreAll: animal-people cap, gate holds, trim countdowns, sw:13036-13070), hunting, curious, scavenging walks, every V7 raw write and forager walks;
    • gives back spill borrows;
    • sets enabled = false;
    • cancels every job;
    • restores irruption writes.
  • off / disable seasonal-wildlife: turn_off → disableSched, plus the aquarium flag and autostart off (sw:16257-16279).
  • All off: PANEL.allOff remembers the switches, runs PANEL.restoreAll (also ends a standing coupling or pattern table, sw:16042-16060), and sets every non-layer switch off. The GUI then calls disableSched (gui:2641); the registry calls reschedule (ctl:913-914).
  • World unload: each restore in its own pcall, every job cancelled, lastSeason = nil (sw:17099-17109).
  • What none of these put back: population quantities and extinct flags, and exhaust / spill assignment edits (spill is given back on disable; exhaust borrows are not). Every out-of-season, inactive or resting entry stays at quantity = 0, extinct = true in the world after disable, with its stock remembered only in the tool's reserve site data. Only resetToDefault (a Roster "reset everything") writes quantities back from the worldgen snapshot (sw:3928-3940).
